1.title: CRDs and Operators
1.text: Welcome to Module thirteen: C R Ds and Operators. It covers the exam area Application Environment, Configuration and Security. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, and every task was run on a real cluster, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do six things. Extending the A P I. Read a C R D (Custom Resource Definition). Discover custom resources. Use custom resources. Operators in practice. Practice with four hands-on labs worth twenty-six points.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Application Environment, Configuration and Security (twenty-five percent). Practice in this module: four labs, twenty-six points, about twenty-seven minutes. Exam format: performance-based tasks in a live terminal, scored on the final cluster state. Validated on: Kubernetes version one point thirty-seven point zero.

1.title: Extending the API
1.text: Extending the A P I. The figure shows this: C R D and operator. Exam tip: A custom resource only stores data; an operator is the controller that acts on it.

1.title: Extending the API, continued
1.text: Extending the A P I. Kubernetes ships kinds such as Pod, Deployment and Service. A Custom Resource Definition (C R D) adds a new kind to the A P I of a running cluster, with no change to Kubernetes itself. After you create the C R D, the A P I server accepts, stores, validates and serves objects of that kind, called custom resources (C R s), and kube control works with them like any other object.

1.title: Extending the API, continued
1.text: Extending the A P I. C R D. the definition of a new kind: group, names, scope, versions and a schema. Custom resource (C R). one object of that kind (a row in the new "table"). Controller. a program that watches objects and makes the real world match them. Operator. a controller plus C R Ds (Custom Resource Definitions) that encode the knowledge of a human operator for one application (a database, a certificate manager).

1.title: Extending the API, continued
1.text: Extending the A P I. A C R on its own is only stored data. An operator is what acts on it. The pattern: you create Database with spec dot replicas three; the operator notices, creates the Stateful Set, Services and backups, and updates status. Well-known operators: cert-manager ( Certificate ), Prometheus Operator ( Service Monitor ), database operators ( Postgres Cluster ), Argo C D ( Application ). Many are installed with Helm or with a manifest that contains the C R Ds, the operator Deployment and its R back.

1.title: Read a CRD
1.text: Read a C R D. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study. Exam tip: A C R D is named plural. group and its objects use api Version group or version.

1.title: Read a CRD, continued
1.text: Read a C R D. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

1.title: Read a CRD, continued
1.text: Read a C R D. The name of a C R D is always plural. group. The api Version of its objects is group or version, here shop dot example dot com slash version one. scope decides whether objects live in a namespace.

1.title: Discover custom resources
1.text: Discover custom resources. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study. Exam tip: Use kube control explain kind dot spec to see the exact fields before you write a custom resource.

1.title: Discover custom resources, continued
1.text: Discover custom resources. kube control explain works for custom resources because the C R D carries the schema. If a C R D has no schema, explain shows little.

1.title: Use custom resources
1.text: Use custom resources. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study. Exam tip: Create the C R D first and wait until it is Established; deleting a C R D deletes all its custom resources.

1.title: Use custom resources, continued
1.text: Use custom resources. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

1.title: Use custom resources, continued
1.text: Use custom resources. Apply a C R before its C R D exists. no matches for kind Widget in version shop dot example dot com slash version one: create the C R D first and wait for Established ( kube control wait the for flag set to condition Established crd or name ). A field breaks the schema. the A P I server rejects it with the path and rule, for example spec dot size Invalid value string spec dot size in body must be of type integer and Unsupported value navy supported values red, green, blue.

1.title: Use custom resources, continued
1.text: Use custom resources. A required field is missing. spec dot size Required value. Cluster-scoped kind. no dash n, no namespace in the manifest. Delete a C R D. all its custom resources are deleted with it. Use kube control explain widget dot spec to see which fields exist and which are required, then fix the manifest.

1.title: Operators in practice
1.text: Operators in practice. Find what an operator added: kube control get crd, then kube control api resources the api group flag set to group. Use it: create a C R. The operator creates ordinary objects; look at them with kube control get all dash n ns and read the C R's status ( kube control get kind name dash o yaml ). If nothing happens: the operator Pod may be down. kube control get pods dash n operator namespace and kube control logs deploy or operator. Install one: usually helm install (Module six) or kube control apply dash f install dot yaml. Create the C R Ds first; the operator Deployment needs the R back (Service Account, Cluster Role, binding) from Module eleven to watch objects.

1.title: Operators in practice, continued
1.text: Operators in practice. An operator reacts to changes continuously (the control loop): if you delete a resource it created, it recreates it. Change the C R, not the generated objects. Exam tip. "Create a custom resource" tasks give a C R D (or tell you it exists) and the field values. Run kube control explain kind dot spec first: it shows the exact field names and types, and saves you from schema errors. Exam tip. Check the scope with kube control api resources the api group flag set to group (namespaced true or false) before you decide whether to use dash n.

1.title: Lab 13.1: crd custom resource
1.text: Lab thirteen point one: crd custom resource. This task is worth seven points, and you should plan about eight minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. The file about slash crd slash crontab crd dot yaml defines a Custom Resource Definition for the kind Cron Tab (group stable dot example dot com ). Install it in the cluster. Then create a Cron Tab custom resource named nightly in the namespace default with spec dot cron Spec zero two and spec dot image backup one dot zero. Finally write the full name of the C R D (the value in the name column of kube control get crd ) to about slash answers slash crd name dot txt. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 13.1: crd custom resource, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control apply dash f about slash crd slash crontab crd dot yaml. Then kube control wait the for flag set to condition Established crd slash crontabs dot stable dot example dot com the timeout flag set to sixty seconds. kube control apply dash f -. The manifest comes next, as shown on the screen. Then kube control get crd then pipe to grep crontabs. Then echo crontabs dot stable dot example dot com about slash answers slash crd name dot txt. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 13.2: discover crds
2.text: Lab thirteen point two: discover crds. This task is worth seven points, and you should plan about seven minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. The cluster has custom resource definitions of several A P I groups. (one) Write the full names of all C R Ds in the A P I group shop dot example dot com, one per line and sorted, to about slash answers slash crds dot txt. (two) In the namespace crd, there are several Widget objects. Write the names of those whose spec dot color is red, one per line and sorted, to about slash answers slash red dot txt. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 13.2: discover crds, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control get crd. Then kube control get crd dash o name grep shop dot example dot com sed s. or sort about slash answers slash crds dot txt. Then kube control dash n crd get widgets dash o json path range dot items? @ dot spec dot color red dot metadata dot name newline end sort about slash answers slash red dot txt. Then cat about slash answers slash crds dot txt about slash answers slash red dot txt. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 13.3: fix custom resource
2.text: Lab thirteen point three: fix custom resource. This task is worth six points, and you should plan about six minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. The C R D for the kind Widget (group shop dot example dot com ) is installed. The manifest about slash work slash widget dot yaml for the Widget blue one in the namespace crd is rejected by the A P I server. Read the error, fix the manifest without changing the name, and create the object. It must end up with spec dot size three and spec dot color blue. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 13.3: fix custom resource, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control apply dash f about slash work slash widget dot yaml two one then pipe to head -five. Then kube control explain widget dot spec. Then make the edit with sed, as shown on the screen. Then kube control apply dash f about slash work slash widget dot yaml. Then kube control dash n crd get widgets. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 13.4: cluster scoped resource
2.text: Lab thirteen point four: cluster scoped resource. This task is worth six points, and you should plan about six minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. The C R D clusterbackups dot data dot example dot com (kind Cluster Backup, group data dot example dot com ) is installed. Find out whether it is namespaced, and create a Cluster Backup named weekly with spec dot target s three or or backups slash weekly. Then write the scope of the C R D ( Namespaced or Cluster ) to about slash answers slash scope dot txt. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 13.4: cluster scoped resource, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control api resources the api group flag set to data dot example dot com. Then kube control get crd clusterbackups dot data dot example dot com dash o json path dot spec dot scope about slash answers slash scope dot txt. kube control apply dash f -. The manifest comes next, as shown on the screen. Then cat about slash answers slash scope dot txt echo. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Recall Check 1
2.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What does a Custom Resource Definition do? Answer: It adds a new kind to the Kubernetes A P I, with a schema, so that objects of that kind can be created. Question two. How is a C R D named? Answer: plural. group, for example widgets dot shop dot example dot com. Question three. What is the difference between a custom resource and an operator? Answer: A custom resource is stored data of the new kind; an operator is a controller that acts on those objects.

2.title: Recall Check 2
2.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Which command lists the custom kinds of one A P I group? Answer: kube control api resources the api group flag set to group. Question five. How do you see the fields of a custom resource? Answer: kube control explain kind dot spec (the C R D's schema). Question six. What happens to the custom resources when you delete their C R D? Answer: They are deleted too.

2.title: Recall Check 3
2.text: Recall check three. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question seven. What error appears if you create a C R before its C R D exists? Answer: no matches for kind... in version.... Question eight. Why do you change the C R and not the objects an operator created? Answer: The operator's control loop restores the objects to match the C R.

2.title: Module Recap
2.text: Here is the recap. C R D: adds a kind; name plural. group; scope Namespaced or Cluster; schema validates. C R: api Version group or version, kind, spec. Operator: controller plus C R Ds; acts on C R s; installed with Helm or a manifest. Discover: get crd, api resources the api group flag, explain, describe crd. Errors: no matches for kind (no C R D), Invalid value, Unsupported value, Required value. Short name: kube control get wd works if the C R D lists short Names. Delete C R D: deletes all its C R s.
